newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy ponders 60 trln lire budget package - papers.
newsitem.headline: Italy ponders 60 trln lire budget package - papers.

text.p: The Italian government is considering a 1997 budget with some 60 trillion lire of deficit reduction measures in two tranches, newspapers said on Thursday.
Il Corriere della Sera daily said the government was preparing a budget of around 38.5 trillion lire in spending cuts and increased revenues immediately.
Then "in the coming months" the government would present an extraordinary "tax for Europe" measure of 22 trillion lire, the daily said.
It said the figures were confirmed by Fabio Mussi, the head of the Democratic Party of Left in the lower house of parliament, and other politicians.
Other newspapers also reported similar figures divided up into two tranches.

La Repubblica newspaper quoted Mussi as saying, "The order of size of the budget that's being studied is 60 trillion but lots of hypotheses are being worked on and among those there is the idea of whether to make the jump in just one leap or in two steps."

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi hinted on Wednesday the budget would try to prune the 1997 deficit by more than the originally planned 32.4 trillion lire but said press reports that a 40 trillion lire package was in the making were exaggerated.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said on Thursday budget measures were still likely to be for around 33 trillion lire, with an additional 3.5 trillion lire to finance a labour pact.

A summit of leaders of parties in the government and the hard left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti to discuss the budget had been due to take place on Wednesday but was put back 24 hours to give Prime Minister Romano Prodi more time for talks with ministers.
The package is due to be presented to parliament by the end of the month.
